description.narrative: (Ethiopia): The Resilience Learning activity (RLA) supports the Transition into Graduation through Enhanced Highlands Resilience (TIGER) project to be more efficient, effective, and transparent in achieving development and resilience outcomes in the chronically vulnerable highlands of Ethiopia through the use of evidence, adaptive management techniques and Collaborating, Learning and Adapting (CLA) practices. .RL will set the stage for scaling and improving the effectiveness of government systems and programs on climate change adaptation activities leading to reductions in chronic vulnerability in Ethiopia by:.Facilitating coordination and collaboration across TIGER partners.Providing relevant research to the TIGER learning agenda.Provide timely field-based measurement.Ensuring iterative planning and action.Supporting data-driven decision-making and innovation...RL will also measure the impact of layering and sequencing multiple USAID investments. Furthermore, RL will support a stakeholder-wide culture of collaborative recognition of successes and failures. RLA is a learning, collaborating, and adapting mechanism for the activities implemented under the highland's resilience project. These activities aim to increase capacity to sustainably diversify own production; increase last-mile supply of nutritious foods and improve knowledge of maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN) practices and demand for health services. The collaborative learning and rapid feedback approach of the RL activity is founded on the principles of local ownership and collective impact to support Ethiopia's journey towards self-reliance. The design of the activity supports a stakeholder-wide culture of collaborative recognition of successes, failures, and areas of uncertainty leading to reductions in chronic vulnerability in Ethiopia........
